title: Canonical section of a Cartier dual ideal under arbitrary Cartier-preserving pullback
statement: Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ and $i':D'\hookrightarrow T'$ be effective Cartier closed immersions [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $v:T'\to T$ and $w:D'\to D$ form a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $\mathcal I_i$ and $\mathcal I_{i'}$ for their ideal sheaves. There is an isomorphism $e:v^*(\mathcal I_i^\vee)\simeq\mathcal I_{i'}^\vee$ from ordinary pullback of the dual ideal that takes the pulled canonical divisor section $s_i$ [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] to the primed section: $e\circ v^*s_i=s_{i'}\circ a_v$, where $a_v:v^*\mathcal O_T\simeq\mathcal O_{T'}$ is the canonical unit comparison. Neither base morphism is assumed flat.

proof.text: The cartesian square identifies the new ideal with the comap ideal. Invertibility on both sides makes the canonical tensor pullback ideal map an isomorphism preserving the ideal inclusion. Use the existing tensor-ideal comparison, not merely an arbitrary line-bundle isomorphism.

The canonical divisor section is the transpose of the ideal inclusion under dual evaluation. Pull back its evaluation identity, use the inclusion compatibility and strong monoidal right unitality, and transpose the resulting square. The canonical tensor-dual comparison is invertible for a line bundle; composing it with the dual of the ideal comparison gives the dual-ideal comparison preserving sections.

Transport the tensor-pullback comparison to ordinary pullback through picardTensorComparison. Naturality at the section and the unit comparison cancel the intermediate comparison maps. The resulting isomorphism has the required section equation.

lean.statement:
theorem cartierPair_pullback_section {D D' T T' : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : D ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i] (hI : i.ker.IsInvertible)
    (i' : D' ⟶ T') [IsClosedImmersion i'] (hI' : i'.ker.IsInvertible)
    (v : T' ⟶ T) (w : D' ⟶ D) (sq : IsPullback w i' i v) :
    ∃ e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback v).obj (Scheme.Modules.dual i.ker.toModules) ≅
        Scheme.Modules.dual i'.ker.toModules,
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback v).map (supportedDivisorSection i) ≫ e.hom =
        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackObjUnitIso v).hom ≫ supportedDivisorSection i'
